opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alyssa Rose (E026) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; role (Analyst) does not own Payroll, so admin is not applicable. Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Alyssa Rose (E026) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted. Contractors with basic training max out at read for any system; requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Alyssa Rose (E026) requested write access to Payroll. The Security agent's note indicates she is a contractor with basic security training; under policy, contractors with basic training max out at read for any system (write requires advanced security training, admin is never allowed for contractors). The requested level (write) exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of read is granted. (Note: HR's note listed her as full-time, but the Security DB record is used for access-level determination, and full-time Analyst does not own Payroll so admin would not apply either way; read is the appropriate grant.)

content.text:
The ticket: Alyssa Rose (E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Two notes conflict:
- HR: full_time Analyst, recommend write.
- Security: contractor with basic training, recommend read.

Access policy: contractors with basic training max out at read. So maximum is read. Requested write is above maximum, grant maximum = read.

Which to trust? The Approver reads the notes. There's a conflict in employment type. Security DB says contractor with basic training. Per policy, contractor can have read or write if advanced security training; basic training means read max. So grant read.

Submit decision: read.
